metadata.title: A Note on Spectral Analysis in automorphic representation theory for $\GL_2$: II

extraction_notes.note: TP1 is titled 'Adelic version of regularization due to Zagier' and reproved here (part (4) is new), so it is origin external with a paper proof; LP4 is introduced 'c.f. [Za82, Section 3]' but proved in adelic form, kept as paper.

Theorems 3.4 and 3.7 are preceded by prose computations that prove only one part each ('we obtain (2) of the following', 'deduce (3) of the following'); these are prose proof nodes pointing at nested claims for parts (2) and (3); the other parts have no proof (theorems marked semi_formal).

nodes.name: Regularized integral by subtraction (definition (1))
nodes.statement: (1) We subtract from $\varphi$ a non integral part $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$, considered to have integral $0$ by abuse of orthogonality, and define $$ \int^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = \int \varphi - \mathcal{E}(\varphi). $$
nodes.statement_short: Regularize by subtracting a non-integrable part $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ deemed to have integral 0.

nodes.name: Regularized integral by residue (definition (2))
nodes.statement: (2) We introduced some suitable meromorphic function $E(s)$ with constant residue $1$ at $0$, such that $$ \int \varphi \cdot E(s) $$ is convergent for certain range of $s$ and has a meromorphic continuation. We then define $$ \int^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = {\rm Res}_{s=0} \int \varphi \cdot E(s). $$
nodes.statement_short: Regularize as the residue at $s=0$ of $\int \varphi E(s)$ for a meromorphic $E(s)$ with residue 1 at 0.

nodes.name: Regularized integral by measure-operator convolution (definition (3))
nodes.statement: (3) We find a/any measure-operator $\sigma_0$ such that the convolution $\sigma_0 * \varphi$ becomes integrable, and that the dual measure $\sigma_0^{\vee}$ with respect to change of variables satisfies $\sigma_0^{\vee} * 1 = R_0 \neq 0$. We then define $$ \int^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = R_0^{-1} \int \sigma_0 * \varphi. $$
nodes.statement_short: Regularize via a measure-operator $\sigma_0$ making $\sigma_0*\varphi$ integrable, normalized by $R_0=\sigma_0^{\vee}*1$.

nodes.name: Singular case
nodes.statement: However, neither \cite{Za82} nor \cite[\S 4.3]{MV10} was capable of explicitly treating an exceptional case (we shall call it the \emph{singular case}), in which $\varphi$ has the quasi-character $\norm_{\ag{A}}$ in its set of exponents \cite[\S 4.3.3]{MV10}.
nodes.statement_short: The singular case: $\varphi$ has the quasi-character $|\cdot|_{\mathbb{A}}$ among its exponents.

nodes.name: Definition (3) fails in the singular case
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that any measure $\sigma_0$ made from Hecke operators which makes the regularizing Eisenstein series integrable also makes $\sigma_0^{\vee}=\sigma_0$ annihilate $1$ (c.f. Remark \ref{KillRegEis}). Hence the definition (3) can not be extended to the singular case.
nodes.statement_short: Any Hecke-operator measure making the regularizing Eisenstein series integrable annihilates 1, so definition (3) fails in the singular case.
assumptions: any measure $\sigma_0$ made from Hecke operators which makes the regularizing Eisenstein series integrable
conclusions: also makes $\sigma_0^{\vee}=\sigma_0$ annihilate $1$
Hence the definition (3) can not be extended to the singular case.

nodes.name: Regularizable function on $\mathbb{R}_+$
nodes.statement: Let $a: \ag{R}_+ \to \ag{C}$ be a continuous function. It is \emph{regularizable} if \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] for any $N \gg 1$ as $t \to \infty$ $$ a(t) = f(t)+O(t^{-N}), \quad f(t)=\sum_{i=1}^l \frac{c_i}{n_i!} t^{\frac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i}t, $$ where $c_i, \alpha_i \in \ag{C}, n_i \in \ag{N}$; \item[(2)] for some $\alpha \in \ag{R}$ as $t \to 0^+$ $$ a(t) = O(t^{\alpha}). $$ \end{itemize} In this case, we write for $T > 0$ $$ h_T(s) = \sum_{i=1}^l \frac{c_i}{n_i!} \frac{\partial^{n_i}}{\partial s^{n_i}} \left( \frac{T^{s+\alpha_i}}{s+\alpha_i} \right) = \sum_{i=1}^l c_i \sum_{m=0}^{n_i} \frac{(-1)^{n_i-m}}{m!} \frac{T^{s+\alpha_i} \log^m T}{(s+\alpha_i)^{n_i-m+1}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: $a$ on $\mathbb{R}_+$ is regularizable if it has a finite log-power asymptotic expansion at $\infty$ and polynomial bound at $0$; defines $h_T(s)$.
nodes.label: RegFuncRDef

nodes.name: Exponent bound for integrable expansions
nodes.statement: For $f(t)$ as above, if $\lim_{T \to \infty} \int_1^T f(t) \frac{dt}{t^2}$ exists, then $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$.
nodes.statement_short: If $\int_1^\infty f(t)dt/t^2$ converges then all exponents satisfy $\Re\alpha_i<1/2$.
conclusions: $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$.
nodes.label: IntExpBd

nodes.statement: \lim_{T \to \infty} \sum c_j T^{i\tau_j} = 0

nodes.name: Circle group $\mathbb{T}$
nodes.statement: Write $\ag{T} = \ag{R} / \ag{Z}$.

nodes.name: Image $[\vec{x}]$ in the torus
nodes.statement: For any $\vec{x} \in \ag{R}^n$, we write by $[\vec{x}]$ its image in $\ag{T}^n$.

nodes.name: Closed subgroup $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$
nodes.statement: Define $$ \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}} = \overline{\lbrace [t\vec{\theta}] : t\in \ag{R} \rbrace}. $$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$ is the closure of the line $\{[t\vec\theta]\}$ in $\mathbb{T}^n$.

nodes.name: Unique ergodicity of linear flows on $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$
nodes.statement: For any $f \in {\rm C}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$, we have $$ \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T f([\vec{x}] + [t.\vec{\theta}]) dt = \int_{\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}} f dm_{\theta} $$ for all $[\vec{x}] \in \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$. Here $dm_{\theta}$ is the normalized Haar measure on $\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Time averages of continuous functions along $[\vec x]+[t\vec\theta]$ converge to the Haar integral on $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$.
conclusions: $$ \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T}\int_0^T f([\vec{x}] + [t.\vec{\theta}]) dt = \int_{\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}} f dm_{\theta} $$ for all $[\vec{x}] \in \ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3

Consider the group of characters ${m Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ of $\ag{T}^n$ given by $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\vec{x}) = e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x}) = e(\sum_{i=1}^n n_i x_i), \vec{n} \in \ag{N}^n, \vec{x} \in \ag{R}^n $$ where $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$. By the duality theorem for locally compact abelian groups, the group of characters ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$ is the quotient of ${m Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ by the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s which vanish on $\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}}$. Obviously, we have $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})=1 \Leftrightarrow e(t\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}) = 1 	ext{ for }  orall t \in \ag{R} \Leftrightarrow \vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}=0. $$ So ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$ are $e_{\vec{n}}$'s modulo the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s with $\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}=0$. Let $[e_{\vec{n}}] 
eq 0$ denote a non trivial equivalence class of $e_{\vec{n}}$ in the quotient group, we calculate $$ \extnorm{  rac{1}{T} \int_0^T [e_{\vec{n}}]( [\vec{x}] + [t\vec{	heta}] ) dt } = \extnorm{  rac{e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x})}{T} \cdot  rac{e(T\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta} ) - 1}{\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}} } \leq  rac{2}{
orm[T] \cdot 
orm[\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}]} 	o 0, T 	o \infty. $$ The lemma is thus proved for $f = [e_{\vec{n}}]$, hence the $\ag{C}$-vector space generated by ${m Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$, which is also a $*$-subalgebra of ${m C}(\ag{T}_{\vec{	heta}})$. The lemma then follows by a standard application of the complex version of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Verify the limit for nontrivial characters by explicit integration, then extend by Stone-Weierstrass.

nodes.name: Characters of the torus
nodes.statement: Consider the group of characters ${\rm Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ of $\ag{T}^n$ given by $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\vec{x}) = e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x}) = e(\sum_{i=1}^n n_i x_i), \vec{n} \in \ag{N}^n, \vec{x} \in \ag{R}^n $$ where $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the characters $e_{\vec n}$ of $\mathbb{T}^n$.

nodes.name: Characters of the subgroup
nodes.statement: By the duality theorem for locally compact abelian groups, the group of characters ${\rm Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$ is the quotient of ${\rm Ch}(\ag{T}^n)$ by the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s which vanish on $\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}}$. Obviously, we have $$ e_{\vec{n}}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})=1 \Leftrightarrow e(t\vec{n} \cdot \vec{\theta}) = 1 \text{ for } \forall t \in \ag{R} \Leftrightarrow \vec{n} \cdot \vec{\theta}=0. $$ So ${\rm Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$ are $e_{\vec{n}}$'s modulo the subgroup of $e_{\vec{n}}$'s with $\vec{n} \cdot \vec{\theta}=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Pontryagin duality identifies the characters of $\mathbb{T}_{\vec\theta}$.

nodes.name: Bound for characters
nodes.statement:
Let $[e_{\vec{n}}] 
eq 0$ denote a non trivial equivalence class of $e_{\vec{n}}$ in the quotient group, we calculate $$ \extnorm{  rac{1}{T} \int_0^T [e_{\vec{n}}]( [\vec{x}] + [t\vec{	heta}] ) dt } = \extnorm{  rac{e(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x})}{T} \cdot  rac{e(T\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta} ) - 1}{\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}} } \leq  rac{2}{
orm[T] \cdot 
orm[\vec{n} \cdot \vec{	heta}]} 	o 0, T 	o \infty. $$
nodes.statement_short: Time average of a nontrivial character tends to 0.

nodes.name: Stone-Weierstrass
nodes.statement: The lemma is thus proved for $f = [e_{\vec{n}}]$, hence the $\ag{C}$-vector space generated by ${\rm Ch}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$, which is also a $*$-subalgebra of ${\rm C}(\ag{T}_{\vec{\theta}})$. The lemma then follows by a standard application of the complex version of the Stone-Weierstrass theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to all continuous functions by Stone-Weierstrass.

nodes.name: Limit of finite sum of $x^{i\theta_k}$ forces constancy
nodes.statement: Consider the function $f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{i \theta_k}, x \in \ag{R}_+$, where $a_k \in \ag{C}, \theta_k \in \ag{R}, 1\leq k \leq n$. If $\lim_{x \to +\infty} f(x)$ exists, then $f(x)$ is a constant function.
nodes.statement_short: A finite sum $\sum a_k x^{i\theta_k}$ with a limit at $+\infty$ is constant.
assumptions: Consider the function $f(x) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k x^{i \theta_k}, x \in \ag{R}_+$, where $a_k \in \ag{C}, \theta_k \in \ag{R}, 1\leq k \leq n$.
conclusions: $f(x)$ is a constant function.
nodes.label: ErgodicLemma

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.4
nodes.statement: Note that $f(e^{2\pi t}) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(t\theta_k), t \in \ag{R}$. If $f$ is not constant, we can find $t_1, t_2 \in \ag{R}$ s.t. $f(e^{2\pi t_1}) \neq f(e^{2\pi t_2})$. By continuity, we then find some neighborhood $U_1$ of $[t_1 \vec{\theta}]$, and $U_2$ of $[t_2 \vec{\theta}]$ such that $$ \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(x_k) \neq \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(y_k), \forall \vec{x} \in U_1, \vec{y} \in U_2. $$ But the flow $\gamma(t) = [t\vec{\theta}]$ meets both $U_1$ and $U_2$ infinitely often by the lemma, hence $\lim_{t \to \infty} f(e^{2\pi t})$ can not exist, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: two distinct values persist in neighbourhoods that the flow visits infinitely often by Lemma 2.3.

nodes.name: Reparametrize
nodes.statement: Note that $f(e^{2\pi t}) = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(t\theta_k), t \in \ag{R}$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $f(e^{2\pi t})$ as a sum of characters.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup
nodes.statement: If $f$ is not constant, we can find $t_1, t_2 \in \ag{R}$ s.t. $f(e^{2\pi t_1}) \neq f(e^{2\pi t_2})$. By continuity, we then find some neighborhood $U_1$ of $[t_1 \vec{\theta}]$, and $U_2$ of $[t_2 \vec{\theta}]$ such that $$ \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(x_k) \neq \sum_{k=1}^n a_k e(y_k), \forall \vec{x} \in U_1, \vec{y} \in U_2. $$
nodes.statement_short: Assume nonconstant; separate values on neighbourhoods $U_1,U_2$.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: But the flow $\gamma(t) = [t\vec{\theta}]$ meets both $U_1$ and $U_2$ infinitely often by the lemma, hence $\lim_{t \to \infty} f(e^{2\pi t})$ can not exist, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: Flow meets both neighbourhoods infinitely often by the lemma, so no limit.

nodes.name: Slowly increasing function
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a continuous function. It is \emph{slowly increasing} if for some $c \in \ag{R}$ and $g$ lying in some Siegel domain we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^c, {\rm Ht}(g) \to \infty. $$
differentia: for some $c \in \ag{R}$ and $g$ lying in some Siegel domain we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^c, {\rm Ht}(g) \to \infty. $$
nodes.label: SlowIncDef

nodes.name: Regularizing kernel $a(t,\varphi)$
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function. Its \emph{regularizing kernel} $a(t,\varphi)$ is $$ a(t,\varphi) = \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A} \times \mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)} \times \gp{K}} \varphi(n(x)a(t^+y)k) dx d^{\times}y dk, $$ where $t^+ = s_{\mathbf{F}}(t)$ is the image of $t$ under the section of the adelic norm map $\ag{A}^{\times} \to \ag{R}_+$ recalled in the beginning of this paper.
nodes.statement_short: $a(t,\varphi)$ averages $\varphi(n(x)a(t^+y)k)$ over $x$, norm-one ideles $y$ and $k\in K$.

nodes.name: Regularizable function on $[{\rm PGL}_2]$ and $R(s,\varphi)$
nodes.statement: We call a slowly increasing function $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ \emph{regularizable} if its regularizing kernel $a(t,\varphi)$ satisfies the condition (1) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}. In this case, we define for $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s \gg 1$ $$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_0^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t}; \quad R^*(s,\varphi) = \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) R(s,\varphi). $$ The space of regularizable functions is denoted by $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi$ is regularizable if its regularizing kernel has a finite asymptotic expansion; defines the Mellin-type $R(s,\varphi)$, $R^*(s,\varphi)$ and the space $\mathcal{A}^{\rm reg}$.
differentia: its regularizing kernel $a(t,\varphi)$ satisfies the condition (1) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}
nodes.label: RegFuncDef

nodes.name: Condition (2) is automatic
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to saying $a(t,\varphi)$ regularizable, i.e., the condition (2) of Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef} is automatically satisfied due to the following Corollary \ref{SIncBdAt0}.

nodes.name: Height bound off the Borel
nodes.statement: If $\gamma \in {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F}) - \gp{B}(\mathbf{F})$, then we have $ {\rm Ht}(\gamma g) \leq {\rm Ht}(g)^{-1}$.
conclusions: $ {\rm Ht}(\gamma g) \leq {\rm Ht}(g)^{-1}$
nodes.label: HtBd

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: This is \cite[Lemma 3.19]{Wu5}.
nodes.statement_short: Citation of [Wu5, Lemma 3.19].

nodes.name: Bound of slowly increasing functions at height $\to 0$
nodes.statement: If $\varphi$ is slowly increasing as in Definition \ref{SlowIncDef}, then we have $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^{\min(0,-c)}, {\rm Ht}(g) \to 0. $$
nodes.statement_short: A slowly increasing $\varphi$ satisfies $|\varphi(g)|\ll {\rm Ht}(g)^{\min(0,-c)}$ as the height tends to 0.
assumptions: $\varphi$ is slowly increasing as in Definition \ref{SlowIncDef}
conclusions: $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^{\min(0,-c)}, {\rm Ht}(g) \to 0. $$
nodes.label: SIncBdAt0

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.10
nodes.statement:
If $c \leq 0$, then it is easy to see that $\varphi$ is bounded, since elements of bounded height in a Siegel domain form a compact subset and $\varphi$ is continuous. The same argument shows that if $c<0$ we can assume $
orm[\varphi(g)] \ll {m Ht}(g)^c$ to hold in a whole Siegel domain $S$ containing a fundamental domain. If ${m Ht}(g)$ is small, we take $\gamma \in {m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})$ such that $\gamma g \in S$, thus by the lemma we get $$ 
orm[\varphi(g)] = 
orm[\varphi(\gamma g)] \ll {m Ht}(\gamma g)^c \leq {m Ht}(g)^{-c}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Boundedness on compact sets, then move $g$ into a Siegel domain by $\gamma$ and apply Lemma 2.9.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: If $c \leq 0$, then it is easy to see that $\varphi$ is bounded, since elements of bounded height in a Siegel domain form a compact subset and $\varphi$ is continuous. The same argument shows that if $c<0$ we can assume $\norm[\varphi(g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(g)^c$ to hold in a whole Siegel domain $S$ containing a fundamental domain.
nodes.statement_short: For $c\le 0$ $\varphi$ is bounded; for $c<0$ the bound holds on a whole Siegel domain.

nodes.name: Apply height lemma
nodes.statement: If ${\rm Ht}(g)$ is small, we take $\gamma \in {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})$ such that $\gamma g \in S$, thus by the lemma we get $$ \norm[\varphi(g)] = \norm[\varphi(\gamma g)] \ll {\rm Ht}(\gamma g)^c \leq {\rm Ht}(g)^{-c}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Translate by $\gamma$ into the Siegel domain and apply the height lemma.

nodes.name: Function $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$ and its Laurent expansion
nodes.statement: \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) := \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(-2s)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2+2s)} = \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)}{s} + \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n)}(0).
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda_F(s)=\Lambda_F(-2s)/\Lambda_F(2+2s)$ with a simple pole at $0$.
nodes.label: lambdaFDef

nodes.name: Truncation operator $\Lambda^c$
nodes.statement: Recall the truncation operator $\Lambda^c$ defined in \cite[(5.5)]{GJ79}.

nodes.name: Spherical section $f_0$
nodes.statement: Let $f_0 \in {\rm Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A}) \cap \gp{K}}^{\gp{K}} (1,1)$ be constant equal to $1$ on $\gp{K}$.

nodes.name: Adelic version of Zagier's regularization
nodes.statement: (Adelic version of regularization due to Zagier \cite{Za82}) \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] Let $\varphi: {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) \to \ag{C}$ be a slowly increasing function. For $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s \gg 1$ and any $T \gg 1$ we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg = \int_0^T a(t,\varphi)t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} - \int_T^{\infty} a(t,\varphi) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s-1/2). $$ \item[(2)] If $\varphi$ is, in addition, regularizable, then we have for $T \gg 1$ \begin{align*} &\quad R^*(s,\varphi) + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) h_T(s) + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s) h_T(-s) \\ &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) \Lambda^T {\rm E}^*(s,f_0)(g) dg + \\ &\quad \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} + \Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{-s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t}. \end{align*} In particular, $R(s,\varphi)$ has a meromorphic continuation to $s \in \ag{C}$ with possible poles at $s=\pm 1/2, \pm \alpha_i, (\rho-1)/2$ for $\rho$ running over the non-trivial zeros of $\zeta_{\mathbf{F}}$, and satisfies the functional equation $$ R^*(s,\varphi) = R^*(-s,\varphi). $$ \item[(3)] Under the condition of (2), if $\Re \alpha_i < 0$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$, then we have $$ R(s,\varphi) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) dg, \quad \max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i < \Re s < -\max_{1 \leq i \leq l} \alpha_i. $$ \item[(4)] Under the condition of (2), if $\varphi$ is integrable on $ [{\rm PGL}_2] := {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})\gp{Z}(\ag{A}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}) $, then we have $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $1 \leq i \leq l$, and $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi(g) dg = \frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} \left( {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=-\frac{1}{2} \\ n_i=0}} \right), \quad {\rm Vol}([{\rm PGL}_2]) = \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0). $$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Rankin-Selberg unfolding against truncated Eisenstein series gives meromorphic continuation and functional equation of $R(s,\varphi)$ and expresses $\int\varphi$ as a residue at $s=1/2$.

nodes.statement:
Since the proofs of (1) to (3) are quite similar to that in \cite{Za82}, we only mention some essential points of them. Only (4) needs more explanation.

For the first term we have  egin{align*} \int_0^T a(t,\varphi) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} + \sum_{i=1}^l  rac{c_i}{n_i!} \int_0^T t^{s+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i} t  rac{dt}{t} \ &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s- rac{1}{2}}  rac{dt}{t} + h_T(s). \end{align*} For the second term we have a similar equality.

We take residue at $s=1/2$ on both sides of the equation obtained in (2) and divide by $\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s)$ to see for $T \gg 1$  egin{align*} &\quad {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} h_T(s) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) h_T(- rac{1}{2}) \ &= \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_{\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g)dg + {m Res}_{s= rac{1}{2}} \int_{\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g) \left( {m E}(s,f_0)(g) - {m E}(s,f_0)_N(g) ight) dg \ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t))  rac{dt}{t^2}, \end{align*} where $\mathcal{D}$ is the standard fundamental domain for $[{m PGL}_2]$ and $\mathcal{D}_T$ is the set of $g \in \mathcal{D}$ such that ${m Ht}(g) \leq T$. nodes.name: Reduction to Zagier
nodes.statement: Since the proofs of (1) to (3) are quite similar to that in \cite{Za82}, we only mention some essential points of them. Only (4) needs more explanation.
nodes.statement_short: Parts (1)-(3) follow Zagier; only (4) is detailed.

nodes.name: Part (1)
nodes.statement: (1) This is standard Rankin-Selberg unfolding together with $$ \Lambda^T {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) = \sum_{\gamma \in \gp{B}(\mathbf{F}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})} f_{0,s}(\gamma g) 1_{{\rm Ht}(\gamma g) \leq T} - \sum_{\gamma \in \gp{B}(\mathbf{F}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F})} \mathcal{M} f_{0,s}(\gamma g) 1_{{\rm Ht}(\gamma g) > T}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Part (1) by Rankin-Selberg unfolding of the truncated Eisenstein series.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: (2) It follows from rewriting the two terms at the right hand side of (1). For the first term we have \begin{align*} \int_0^T a(t,\varphi) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} + \sum_{i=1}^l \frac{c_i}{n_i!} \int_0^T t^{s+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i} t \frac{dt}{t} \\ &= R(s,\varphi) - \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) t^{s-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t} + h_T(s). \end{align*} For the second term we have a similar equality.
nodes.statement_short: Part (2) by rewriting the two terms of (1) via $h_T(s)$.

nodes.name: Part (3)
nodes.statement: (3) In the case $\Re \alpha_i < 0$ for all $i$, we let $T \to \infty$, taking into account Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi} and $h_T(s) \to 0$, to get the asserted equation.
nodes.statement_short: Part (3) by letting $T\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Part (4)
nodes.statement: (4) The integrability of $\varphi$ implies $\Re \alpha_i < 1/2$ for all $i$ by Lemma \ref{IntExpBd}. We take residue at $s=1/2$ on both sides of the equation obtained in (2) and divide by $\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s)$ to see for $T \gg 1$ \begin{align*} &\quad {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} h_T(s) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) h_T(-\frac{1}{2}) \\ &= \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_{\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g)dg + {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} \int_{\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g) \left( {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) - {\rm E}(s,f_0)_N(g) \right) dg \\ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0) \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) \frac{dt}{t^2}, \end{align*} where $\mathcal{D}$ is the standard fundamental domain for $[{\rm PGL}_2]$ and $\mathcal{D}_T$ is the set of $g \in \mathcal{D}$ such that ${\rm Ht}(g) \leq T$. It is easy to see that as $T \to \infty$ $$ h_T(-\frac{1}{2}) \to 0; \quad \int_T^{\infty} (a(t,\varphi)-f(t)) \frac{dt}{t^2} \to 0. $$ By Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi}, ${\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) - {\rm E}(s,f_0)_N(g)$ is of uniformly rapid decay with respect to ${\rm Ht}(g), g \in \mathcal{D}$ as $s$ remains in a compact neighborhood of $1/2$. Hence $$ \int_{\mathcal{D}-\mathcal{D}_T} \varphi(g) \left( {\rm E}(s,f_0)(g) - {\rm E}(s,f_0)_N(g) \right) dg $$ is holomorphic at $s=1/2$. We compute ${\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} h_T(s)$ by noting that the second summand of $$ \frac{d^n}{d s^n} \left( \frac{T^s}{s} \right) = \frac{(-1)^n n!}{s^{n+1}} + \int_0^{\log T} t^n e^{st} dt $$ is holomorphic at $s=0$, and get $$ {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} h_T(s) = c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=-\frac{1}{2} \\ n_i=0}}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Part (4): take residues at $s=1/2$ in (2) and let $T\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Regularized integral on $[{\rm PGL}_2]$
nodes.statement: We define the \emph{regularized integral} of a regularizable function $\varphi: [{\rm PGL}_2] \to \ag{C}$ as $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi(g) dg = \frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} \left( {\rm Res}_{s=\frac{1}{2}} R(s,\varphi) + c_i \delta_{\substack{\alpha_i=-\frac{1}{2} \\ n_i=0}} \right), $$ where $c_i, \alpha_i, n_i$ are associated with $a(t,\varphi)$ as in Definition \ref{RegFuncRDef}. We call the first term the \emph{principal part} of the regularized integral, the second the \emph{degenerate part} of the regularized integral. The regularized integral is linear and extends the integral on $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2) \cap {\rm L}^1({\rm GL}_2, 1)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\int^{\rm reg}\varphi$ = (residue of $R(s,\varphi)$ at $1/2$ + degenerate term) / ${\rm Vol}$; principal and degenerate parts.
nodes.label: RegIntDef

nodes.name: Finitely regularizable function
nodes.statement:
Let $\omega$ be a unitary character of $\mathbf{F}^{	imes}  ackslash \ag{A}^{	imes}$. Let $\varphi$ be a smooth function on ${m GL}_2(\mathbf{F})  ackslash {m GL}_2(\ag{A})$ with central character $\omega$. We call $\varphi$ \emph{finitely regularizable} if there exist characters $\chi_i: \mathbf{F}^{	imes}  ackslash \ag{A}^{	imes} 	o \ag{C}^{(1)}$, $\alpha_i \in \ag{C}, n_i \in \ag{N}$ and smooth functions $f_i \in {m Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A}) \cap \gp{K}}^{\gp{K}} (\chi_i, \omega \chi_i^{-1})$ for $1 \leq i \leq l$, such that for any $M \gg 1$ $$ \varphi(n(x)a(y)k) = \varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(n(x)a(y)k) + O(
orm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{-M}), 	ext{ as } 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}} 	o \infty, $$ where we have written the \emph{essential constant term} $$ \varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(n(x)a(y)k)=\varphi_{\gp{N}}^*(a(y)k)=\sum_{i=1}^l \chi_i(y) 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \log^{n_i} 
orm[y]_{\ag{A}} f_i(k). $$ In this case, we call $\mathcal{E}{m x}(\varphi)=\{ \chi_i 
orm^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i}: 1 \leq i \leq l \}$ the \emph{exponent set} of $\varphi$, and define $$ \mathcal{E}{m x}^+(\varphi) = \{ \chi_i 
orm^{ rac{1}{2}+\alpha_i} \in \mathcal{E}{m x}(\varphi): \Re \alpha_i \geq 0 \}; \quad \mathcal{E}{m x}^-(\varphi) = \{ \chi_i

nodes.name: Finitely regularizable vs regularizable
nodes.statement: In the case $\omega=1$, a finitely regularizable is smooth and regularizable in the sense of Definition \ref{RegFuncDef}. But a smooth regularizable function doesn't need to be finitely regularizable.

nodes.name: Regularizing Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: In the case $\omega^{-1}\xi^2(t)=\norm[t]_{\ag{A}}^{i\mu}$ for some $\mu \in \ag{R}$, we introduce the \emph{regularizing Eisenstein series} for $f \in V_{\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ and $s$ in a neighborhood of $(1-i\mu)/2$ $$ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(s,f)(g) = {\rm E}(s,f)(g) - \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-i\mu)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+i\mu)} \int_{\gp{K}} f(\kappa) d\kappa \cdot \chi^{-1}(\det g) \norm[\det g]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{i\mu}{2}}. $$ It is holomorphic at $s=(1-i\mu)/2$.
nodes.statement_short: ${\rm E}^{\rm reg}(s,f)$ subtracts from ${\rm E}(s,f)$ the pole-carrying character term, making it holomorphic at $s=(1-i\mu)/2$.
nodes.label: RegEisDef

nodes.name: Hecke operators and the regularizing Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: Let $e_0 \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$ be the spherical function taking value $1$ on $\gp{K}$. Let $T(\mathfrak{p})$ denote the order $1$ Hecke operator at a finite place $\mathfrak{p}$ with cardinality of the residue field $q$. For $s \neq 0$, we have $$ T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) = \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0), \quad \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) = \frac{q^{1/2+s} + q^{-(1/2+s)}}{q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}}; $$ $$ \text{or} \quad T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) = \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s) {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s, e_0) + (\lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s)-1) \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s). $$ The pole of $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$, defined in (\ref{lambdaFDef}), at $s=0$ is compensated by the zero of $\lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}(s)-1$, hence we get $$ T(\mathfrak{p}). {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, e_0) = {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, e_0) + \lambda_{\mathfrak{p}}^{(1)}(0) \cdot \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0). $$ In particular, $(T(\mathfrak{p})-1)^2$ annihilates ${\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2,e_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: $T(\mathfrak{p})$ acts on ${\rm E}^{\rm reg}(1/2,e_0)$ as identity plus a constant, so $(T(\mathfrak{p})-1)^2$ annihilates it.
nodes.label: KillRegEis

nodes.name: Violation of covariance
nodes.statement: {(Violation of Covariance)} Unlike the usual Eisenstein series, the map $$ \pi^{\infty}(\xi \norm^{(1-i\mu)/2}, \omega\xi^{-1} \norm^{-(1-i\mu)/2}) \to {\rm C}^{\infty}({\rm GL}_2, \omega), \quad f_{(1-i\mu)/2} \mapsto {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}((1-i\mu)/2, f) $$ is \emph{NOT} ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$-covariant. But it's still $\gp{K}$-covariant.

nodes.name: Examples of finitely regularizable functions
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi}, \ref{GlobRDEisCst} and the definition of cusp forms, $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ contains: \begin{itemize} \item $\chi(\det g)$ for quasi-characters $\chi$ such that $\chi^2=\omega$; \item smooth cusp forms, i.e., $\mathcal{A}_{{\rm cusp}}^{\infty}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n}{\rm E}(s,f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and smooth $f \in {\rm Ind}_{\gp{B}(\ag{A})}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})}(\xi, \omega\xi^{-1})$ with $\Re s \geq 0$ and $s \neq -i\mu/2, 1/2-i\mu/2$ for $\mu=\mu(\omega^{-1}\xi^2)$ if $\omega\xi^{-2}$ is trivial on $\ag{A}^{(1)}$; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=-i\frac{\mu}{2}} (s+i\frac{\mu}{2}){\rm E}^*(s,f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and smooth $f$, $\mu$ the same as above; \item $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n}{\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1-i\mu}{2},f)$ for some $n \in \ag{N}$ and $f,\mu$ the same as above; \item $\varphi=\Pi_{j=1}^l \varphi_j$ where $\varphi_j \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega_j)$ with $\omega = \Pi_j \omega_j$. \end{itemize} In the last case, we have $ \varphi_{\gp{N}}^* = \Pi_j \varphi_{j,\gp{N}}^* $. Note that we have excluded ${\rm E}(s,f)$ for $\Re s < 0$. But they are actually present since they are related to the case $\Re s > 0$ by functional equation.
nodes.statement_short: Lists members of $\mathcal{A}^{\rm fr}$: characters, cusp forms, derivatives of (regularizing) Eisenstein series and products.

nodes.name: ${\rm L}^2$-residual space
nodes.statement: Let $\omega$ be a unitary character of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$. The ${\rm L}^2$-\emph{residual space} of central character $\omega$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$, is the direct sum of the vector spaces $\mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ resp. $\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ spanned by functions $$ \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f), \text{if } s \neq \frac{1-i\mu}{2} \quad \text{resp.} \quad \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1-i\mu}{2},f) $$ where $s \in \ag{C}, \Re s > 0$ and for some unitary character $\xi$ of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$, $f \in V_{\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ and $\mu$ as above.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is spanned by $s$-derivatives of Eisenstein series and of regularizing Eisenstein series with $\Re s>0$.

nodes.name: Translation stability of $\mathcal{A}^{\rm fr}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$. Moreover, for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ and any $g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, their sets of exponents are the same: $$ \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(g.\varphi) = \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi). $$
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{A}^{\rm fr}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is stable under right translation, preserving exponent sets.
assumptions: for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ and any $g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$
conclusions: $\mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm GL}_2,\omega)$ is stable under the right translation by ${\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.21
nodes.statement: Take a flat section $f_s$ as in the proof of Proposition \ref{FregStab}. Fix $s_0 \in \ag{C}, n \in \ag{N}, g \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$ with $\Re s_0 > 0$. Let $e_{\vec{k}}$ be an orthonormal $\gp{K}$-isotypic basis of ${\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi, \omega\xi^{-1})$. There is an orthonormal $\gp{K}$-isotypic basis $\tilde{e}_{\vec{k}}$ of ${\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\omega\xi^{-1}, \xi)$ and for any $n \in \ag{N}$ there is $A > 0$ such that (c.f. \cite[\S 3]{Wu5}) $$ \mathcal{M}_s e_{\vec{k},s} = \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}, \quad \extnorm{\mu_{\vec{k}}^{(n)}(s)} \ll \lambda_{\vec{k}}^A $$ for some meromorphic function $\mu_{\vec{k}}(s)$, regular in $\Re s > 0, s \neq 1/2$. Here $\lambda_{\vec{k}}$ is the eigenvalue of the Laplacian on $\gp{K}_{\infty}$ for $e_{\vec{k}}$, and the bound is uniform for $s$ lying in any compact subset of the regular region. We also have an expansion $$ g.f_s = \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) e_{\vec{k},s}, $$ for some functions $a_{\vec{k}}(s,g)$ holomorphic in $s$ and smooth in $g$, since $$ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) = \int_{\gp{K}} f_s(\kappa g) \overline{e_{\vec{k}}(\kappa)} d\kappa. $$ Moreover, we have $ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N} $ for any $N \in \ag{N}$, uniformly for $s$ lying in any compact neighborhood of $s_0$. It follows that for any $l \in \ag{N}$ $$ a_{\vec{k}}^{(l)}(s,g) := \frac{\partial^l}{\partial s^l} \mid_{s=s_0} a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N}. $$ We thus get $$ g.f_{s_0}^{(n)} = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k},s_0}^{(k)}. $$ The inner sum coincides with the value at $s=s_0$ of a flat section $f_{k,s}^{(k)}$ defined by $$ f_k = \binom{n}{k} \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k}}, $$ which is smooth. We can also verify that \begin{align*} \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_{k,s} &= \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} (\mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) \\ &= \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} (a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_s, \end{align*} hence we deduce that $$ g.{\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k). $$ We conclude by $$ g.{\rm E}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k) $$ since both sides are orthogonal to the cusp forms and have the same constant term.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the translated flat section in a $K$-isotypic basis with rapidly decaying coefficients, apply the intertwining operator termwise, and compare constant terms.

nodes.name: Intertwining bounds
nodes.statement: There is an orthonormal $\gp{K}$-isotypic basis $\tilde{e}_{\vec{k}}$ of ${\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\omega\xi^{-1}, \xi)$ and for any $n \in \ag{N}$ there is $A > 0$ such that (c.f. \cite[\S 3]{Wu5}) $$ \mathcal{M}_s e_{\vec{k},s} = \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}, \quad \extnorm{\mu_{\vec{k}}^{(n)}(s)} \ll \lambda_{\vec{k}}^A $$ for some meromorphic function $\mu_{\vec{k}}(s)$, regular in $\Re s > 0, s \neq 1/2$. nodes.name: Rapid decay of coefficients
nodes.statement: We also have an expansion $$ g.f_s = \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) e_{\vec{k},s}, $$ for some functions $a_{\vec{k}}(s,g)$ holomorphic in $s$ and smooth in $g$, since $$ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) = \int_{\gp{K}} f_s(\kappa g) \overline{e_{\vec{k}}(\kappa)} d\kappa. $$ Moreover, we have $ a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N} $ for any $N \in \ag{N}$, uniformly for $s$ lying in any compact neighborhood of $s_0$. It follows that for any $l \in \ag{N}$ $$ a_{\vec{k}}^{(l)}(s,g) := \frac{\partial^l}{\partial s^l} \mid_{s=s_0} a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \ll_{g,f,N} \lambda_{\vec{k}}^{-N}. $$

nodes.name: Define $f_k$
nodes.statement: We thus get $$ g.f_{s_0}^{(n)} = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k},s_0}^{(k)}. $$ The inner sum coincides with the value at $s=s_0$ of a flat section $f_{k,s}^{(k)}$ defined by $$ f_k = \binom{n}{k} \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) e_{\vec{k}}, $$ which is smooth.
nodes.statement_short: Write the translate as a sum of derivatives of smooth flat sections $f_k$.

nodes.name: Constant terms
nodes.statement: We can also verify that \begin{align*} \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_{k,s} &= \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \binom{n}{k} a_{\vec{k}}^{(n-k)}(s_0,g) \frac{\partial^k}{\partial s^k} \mid_{s=s_0} (\mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) \\ &= \sideset{}{_{\vec{k}}} \sum \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} (a_{\vec{k}}(s,g) \mu_{\vec{k}}(s) \tilde{e}_{\vec{k},-s}) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=s_0} \mathcal{M}_s f_s, \end{align*} hence we deduce that $$ g.{\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k). $$
nodes.statement_short: Same relation for intertwined sections, hence for constant terms.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We conclude by $$ g.{\rm E}^{(n)}(s_0,f) = \sideset{}{_{k=0}^n} \sum {\rm E}^{(k)}(s_0,f_k) $$ since both sides are orthogonal to the cusp forms and have the same constant term.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude since both sides are orthogonal to cusp forms with equal constant terms.

nodes.name: The two constructions of $f_k$ coincide

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.24
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{IntExpBd} and Proposition \ref{GlobRDEisWhi}, it is not difficult to see that $\mathcal{E}({\rm GL}_2,\omega) \cap {\rm L}^2({\rm GL}_2(\mathbf{F}) \backslash {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A}), \omega) = \{0\}$, which implies the uniqueness of $\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ in (2). For the existence, we find $\chi_i, \alpha_i, n_i, f_i$ as in Definition \ref{FinRegFuncDef}. Then we take, writing $\mu_i = \mu(\omega^{-1}\chi_i^2)$, \begin{equation} \mathcal{E}(\varphi) = \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j \neq \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j) + \sum_{\substack{\Re \alpha_j > 0 \\ \alpha_j = \frac{1}{2}+i\mu_j}} \frac{\partial^{n_j}}{\partial s^{n_j}}{\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\alpha_j,\omega,\omega^{-1}\chi_j;f_j). \end{equation} Thus for any $\chi \in \mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi))$, we have $\Re \chi \leq 1/2$ resp. $\Re \chi < 1/2$ under the condition in (2). Hence $\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$ resp. ${\rm L}^2({\rm GL}_2, \omega)$. For the ``moreover'' part, it suffices to see that the differential operator $X$ does not increase the real part of elements in $\mathcal{E}{\rm x}(\varphi)$, which is essentially due to the following calculation: $$ y \frac{d}{dy} (y^{\sigma} \log^k y) = y^{\sigma} \log^k y + k y^{\sigma} \log^{k-1}y, \forall y>0, \sigma \in \ag{C}, k \in \ag{N}. $$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.26

We calculate $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ for $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(gg_0)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$ resp. $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$ for some $f \in V_{\chi,\chi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ with $\Re s > 0$, a unitary character $\chi$ of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$ if $\chi \mid_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} = 1$. Due to the integral $\int_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} d^{\times}y$, it is easy to see that $a(t,\varphi)$ is non-vanishing only if $\chi$ is trivial on $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}$, in which case $\mu(\omega\chi^2)=2\mu(\chi)$. We also notice that we can interchange the order of $\mathcal{M}$ and $\int_{\gp{K}} dk$ since they commute with each other. \begin{itemize} \item $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(g)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$: We get $$ a(t,\mathcal{E}) = \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \left\{ t^{\frac{1}{2}+s+i\mu(\chi)} \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \left( t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)} \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\}, $$ and conclude by the fact that $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ has no constant term as a function of $t$. \item $\mathcal{E}(g)=\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$: We get \begin{align*} a(t,\mathcal{E}) &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi)} \left( (t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)}-1) \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\} \\ &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \sum_{l=0}^n \binom{n}{l} \frac{(-1)^l}{l+1} \cdot \log^{l+1}t \cdot \frac{d^{n-l}}{d s^{n-l}} \mid_{s=0} \left( \frac{s\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2s)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2-2s)} \right) \right\}, \end{align*} and conclude the same way as in the previous case. \end{itemize} For (2), the first part is trivial. For the second part, we note that $\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ implies $g_0.\varphi-g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ for any $g_0 \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, and $g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ has regularized integral $0$ by (1) if either $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,1)$ or $g_0 \in \gp{K}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the regularizing kernel of each type of residual element and observe it has no constant term; (2) then follows by linearity and translation.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: For (1), the second assertion follows from the first by Proposition \ref{Reis+Stab}. We calculate $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ for $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(gg_0)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$ resp. $\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$ for some $f \in V_{\chi,\chi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ with $\Re s > 0$, a unitary character $\chi$ of $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$ if $\chi \mid_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} = 1$. Due to the integral $\int_{\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}} d^{\times}y$, it is easy to see that $a(t,\varphi)$ is non-vanishing only if $\chi$ is trivial on $\mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{(1)}$, in which case $\mu(\omega\chi^2)=2\mu(\chi)$. We also notice that we can interchange the order of $\mathcal{M}$ and $\int_{\gp{K}} dk$ since they commute with each other.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to computing $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ for the two types of residual generators.

nodes.name: Case: Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: \item $\mathcal{E}(g) = \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}(s,f)(g)$ with $s \neq 1/2-i\mu(\chi)$: We get $$ a(t,\mathcal{E}) = \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \left\{ t^{\frac{1}{2}+s+i\mu(\chi)} \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \left( t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)} \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\}, $$ and conclude by the fact that $a(t,\mathcal{E})$ has no constant term as a function of $t$.
nodes.statement_short: Eisenstein derivative case: the kernel has no constant term.

nodes.name: Case: regularizing Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: \item $\mathcal{E}(g)=\frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi),f)(g)$: We get \begin{align*} a(t,\mathcal{E}) &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \frac{\partial^n}{\partial s^n} \mid_{s=\frac{1}{2}-i\mu(\chi)} \left( (t^{\frac{1}{2}-s-i\mu(\chi)}-1) \frac{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1-2s-2i\mu(\chi))}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(1+2s+2i\mu(\chi))} \right) \right\} \\ &= \zeta_{\mathbf{F}}^*(1) \int_{\gp{K}} f(k)dk \cdot \\ &\quad \left\{ t \log^n t + \sum_{l=0}^n \binom{n}{l} \frac{(-1)^l}{l+1} \cdot \log^{l+1}t \cdot \frac{d^{n-l}}{d s^{n-l}} \mid_{s=0} \left( \frac{s\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2s)}{\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(2-2s)} \right) \right\}, \end{align*} and conclude the same way as in the previous case.
nodes.statement_short: Regularizing Eisenstein case: same conclusion.

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: For (2), the first part is trivial. For the second part, we note that $\varphi-\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ implies $g_0.\varphi-g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi) \in {\rm L}^1$ for any $g_0 \in {\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})$, and $g_0.\mathcal{E}(\varphi)$ has regularized integral $0$ by (1) if either $\mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}^+({\rm GL}_2,1)$ or $g_0 \in \gp{K}$.
nodes.statement_short: Part (2) by translating and applying (1).

nodes.name: Comparison with Michel-Venkatesh
nodes.statement: The above proof of (2) is to be compared with \cite[\S 4.3.6]{MV10}, where another simpler but indirect proof was given for the ``regular case''.

nodes.name: Vanishing of regularized products in the regular case
nodes.statement: Let $\xi_j,\xi_j'$ be (unitary) Hecke characters with $\xi_1\xi_1' \xi_2 \xi_2' = 1$ and write $\pi_j = \pi(\xi_j,\xi_j')$, $j=1,2$. For $f_j \in \pi_j$, we shall write ${\rm E}^{\sharp}$ for ${\rm E}$ or ${\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}$, whichever is regular at $s=1/2$. If $\pi_1 \not \simeq \widetilde{\pi_2}$, then for any $n_1, n_2 \in \ag{N}$, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(n_1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(0,f_2) = 0, \quad \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_1)}(1/2,f_1) {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_2)}(1/2,f_2) = 0. $$
nodes.statement_short: If $\pi_1\not\simeq\widetilde{\pi_2}$, regularized integrals of products of derivatives of two Eisenstein series at $0$ or $1/2$ vanish.
assumptions: Let $\xi_j,\xi_j'$ be (unitary) Hecke characters with $\xi_1\xi_1' \xi_2 \xi_2' = 1$ and write $\pi_j = \pi(\xi_j,\xi_j')$, $j=1,2$.
nodes.label: SimpleProd

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: $R(s, {\rm E}^{(n_1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(0,f_2))$ resp. $R(s, {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_1)}(1/2,f_1) {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_2)}(1/2,f_2))$ represents the value at $s_1=s_2=0$ of $\partial_1^{n_1} \partial_2^{n_2}$ of $$ \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2') \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \Lambda(3/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(-1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2'), $$ which is regular at $s=1/2$ by assumption. The degenerate part is also easily seen to be $0$ by assumption. We conclude by Definition \ref{RegIntDef}.
nodes.statement_short: $R(s,\cdot)$ is a product of four completed $L$-functions, regular at $s=1/2$ by assumption; degenerate part vanishes.

nodes.name: Principal and degenerate parts
nodes.statement: $R(s, {\rm E}^{(n_1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(n_2)}(0,f_2))$ resp. $R(s, {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_1)}(1/2,f_1) {\rm E}^{\sharp,(n_2)}(1/2,f_2))$ represents the value at $s_1=s_2=0$ of $\partial_1^{n_1} \partial_2^{n_2}$ of $$ \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2') \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \Lambda(3/2+s+s_1+s_2, \xi_1\xi_2) \Lambda(1/2+s+s_1-s_2, \xi_1\xi_2') \Lambda(1/2+s-s_1+s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2) \Lambda(-1/2+s-s_1-s_2, \xi_1'\xi_2'), $$ which is regular at $s=1/2$ by assumption. The degenerate part is also easily seen to be $0$ by assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Identify $R(s,\cdot)$ with a product of $L$-functions regular at $1/2$; degenerate part is 0.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We conclude by Definition \ref{RegIntDef}.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by the definition of the regularized integral.

nodes.name: Deformation principle
nodes.statement: In general, if $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm PGL}_2), \mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm PGL}_2)$ are given, so that $\varphi - \mathcal{E} \in {\rm L}^1([{\rm PGL}_2])$, and if we can find continuous families $\varphi_s \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm PGL}_2), \mathcal{E}_s \in \mathcal{E}({\rm PGL}_2)$ which coincide with $\varphi, \mathcal{E}$ at $s=0$, then we have \begin{equation} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi - \mathcal{E} = \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi_s - \mathcal{E}_s = \lim_{s \to 0} \left( \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi_s - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}_s \right). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If continuous families $\varphi_s,\mathcal{E}_s$ deform $\varphi,\mathcal{E}$, the regularized integral of $\varphi$ is the limit of differences of regularized integrals.
assumptions: if $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm PGL}_2), \mathcal{E} \in \mathcal{E}({\rm PGL}_2)$ are given, so that $\varphi - \mathcal{E} \in {\rm L}^1([{\rm PGL}_2])$
if we can find continuous families $\varphi_s \in \mathcal{A}^{{\rm fr}}({\rm PGL}_2), \mathcal{E}_s \in \mathcal{E}({\rm PGL}_2)$ which coincide with $\varphi, \mathcal{E}$ at $s=0$
conclusions: \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi - \mathcal{E} = \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi_s - \mathcal{E}_s = \lim_{s \to 0} \left( \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi_s - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}_s \right).

nodes.name: Deformation formula
nodes.statement: \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi - \mathcal{E} = \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi_s - \mathcal{E}_s = \lim_{s \to 0} \left( \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi_s - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}_s \right).
nodes.statement_short: Regularized integral as a limit of differences of regularized integrals along a deformation.
nodes.label: DeformTec

nodes.name: Normalized intertwining operator $\mathcal{M}_s$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_s$
nodes.statement: If $f \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2)$, we define for any $s \in \ag{C}$ an operator $\mathcal{M}_s: {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2) \to {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi_2,\xi_1)$ (abuse of notations) by requiring $$ \mathcal{M}_s f_s(a(y)\kappa) = \xi_2(y)\norm[y]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{1}{2}-s} \mathcal{M}_sf(\kappa), \quad \text{i.e.,} \quad \mathcal{M}_s f_s = (\mathcal{M}_s f)_{-s}; $$ $$ \text{resp.} \quad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_s = \mathcal{M}_s \circ (I-{\rm P}_{\gp{K}}e_{\xi}), \quad \text{if } \xi_1=\xi_2=\xi $$ with the Taylor expansion at $s=0$ resp. $s=1/2$ when $\xi_1=\xi_2 = \xi$ (since $\mathcal{M}_s$ is ``diagonalizable'') $$ \mathcal{M}_sf = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \mathcal{M}_0^{(n)}f, \quad \text{resp.} \quad \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2+s} f = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{s^n}{n!} \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(n)}f. $$ Here ${\rm P}_{\gp{K}}$, with $d\kappa$ the probability Haar measure on $\gp{K}$, is defined to be the map $$ \pi(\xi,\xi) \to \ag{C}, f \mapsto \int_{\gp{K}} f(\kappa) \xi^{-1}(\kappa) d\kappa, $$ and $e_{\xi} = \xi \circ \det \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(\xi,\xi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Defines $\mathcal{M}_s$ on $K$-restrictions via $\mathcal{M}_sf_s=(\mathcal{M}_sf)_{-s}$, its Taylor coefficients, $\widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_s$, ${\rm P}_K$ and $e_\xi$.

nodes.name: Vanishing product (unitary deformation)
nodes.statement: Let $f_1,f_2 \in {\rm Res}_{\gp{K}}^{{\rm GL}_2(\ag{A})} \pi(1,1)$. For $0 \neq s \in \ag{C}$ small, we have $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(s,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = 0. $$
nodes.label: SimpleProdU

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: This is a variant of Lemma \ref{SimpleProd}.
nodes.statement_short: Variant of Lemma 3.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4 (2)
nodes.statement: We continue to use the notations in the previous lemma. We can write $$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,f_1) {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = 2(f_1f_2)_{1/2+s}^{(1)} + 2(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2)_{1/2-s}^{(1)} + (f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2+s} + (\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2-s}. $$ We tentatively define \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) &:= s^{-1} \left\{ 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2+s, f_1f_2) + 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\ &\left. + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2+s, f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\} \end{align*} Applying Lemma \ref{SimpleProdU}, \ref{SimpleProdSing} with $n=0, 1$ together with (\ref{DeformTec}), we get \begin{align*} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) &= \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} s^{-1} {\rm E}(s,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \\ &= \frac{1}{s} \cdot \left\{ 2 \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) + 2 \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\ &\left. + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\}. \end{align*} Taking Laurent expansions, we verify that the function in $s$ in the range of the above limit is regular at $s=0$, unlike its appearance. The properties $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_2) = {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_1), \forall k \in \ag{N}; \quad \mathcal{M}_0^{(2)} = \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} \circ \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} $$ $$ \text{coming from} \quad \mathcal{M}_s \circ \mathcal{M}_{-s} = 1 $$ must be used. Taking limit as $s \to 0$, we obtain (2) of the following:
nodes.statement_short: Deformation: replace ${\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1)$ by $s^{-1}{\rm E}(s,f_1)$, subtract an explicit regularizing residue, apply Lemmas 3.3 and 3.6, and let $s\to 0$ using Laurent expansions and $\mathcal{M}_s\mathcal{M}_{-s}=1$.

nodes.name: Constant term of the product
nodes.statement: We continue to use the notations in the previous lemma. We can write $$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,f_1) {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = 2(f_1f_2)_{1/2+s}^{(1)} + 2(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2)_{1/2-s}^{(1)} + (f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2+s} + (\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2)_{1/2-s}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Write the product of constant terms.

nodes.name: Deformation
nodes.statement: We tentatively define \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) &:= s^{-1} \left\{ 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2+s, f_1f_2) + 2 {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\ &\left. + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2+s, f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(1/2-s, \mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\} \end{align*} Applying Lemma \ref{SimpleProdU}, \ref{SimpleProdSing} with $n=0, 1$ together with (\ref{DeformTec}), we get \begin{align*} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) &= \lim_{s \to 0} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} s^{-1} {\rm E}(s,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \\ &= \frac{1}{s} \cdot \left\{ 2 \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) + 2 \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(1)}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1f_2) \right. \\ &\left. + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(-s)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_s f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define the deforming residual term and apply Lemmas 3.3, 3.6 with the deformation formula.

nodes.name: Regularity at $s=0$
nodes.statement: Taking Laurent expansions, we verify that the function in $s$ in the range of the above limit is regular at $s=0$, unlike its appearance. The properties $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_2) = {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0^{(k)}f_1), \forall k \in \ag{N}; \quad \mathcal{M}_0^{(2)} = \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} \circ \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} $$ $$ \text{coming from} \quad \mathcal{M}_s \circ \mathcal{M}_{-s} = 1 $$ must be used.
nodes.statement_short: Check regularity at $s=0$ using symmetry and $\mathcal{M}_s\mathcal{M}_{-s}=1$.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.statement: Taking limit as $s \to 0$, we obtain (2) of the following:
nodes.statement_short: Take the limit $s\to 0$.

nodes.name: Regularized product of two unitary Eisenstein series
nodes.statement: If $\pi(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is spherical, we also write The regularized integral of the product of two unitary Eisenstein series is computed as: \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] If $\pi_1 = \pi(\xi_1,\xi_2), \pi_2 = \pi(\xi_1^{-1}, \xi_2^{-1})$ resp. $\pi_2 = \pi(\xi_2^{-1}, \xi_1^{-1})$ and $\xi_1 \neq \xi_2$, then $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(0,f_1) {\rm E}(0,f_2) = \frac{2\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2), \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} ({\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2) + {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1)) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2). $$ \item[(2)] If $\pi_1 = \pi(\xi,\xi), \pi_2 = \pi(\xi^{-1},\xi^{-1})$, then \begin{align*} &\quad \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2) = \frac{4\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(2)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) + \frac{4\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(2)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)} f_2) \\ &\quad + \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{-1}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) - \frac{1}{3} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(3)}f_1 \cdot f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(2)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2). \end{align*} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Explicit formulas for the regularized integral of products of two unitary Eisenstein series (or their first derivatives) in terms of ${\rm P}_K$ of intertwined sections.
conclusions: $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}(0,f_1) {\rm E}(0,f_2) = \frac{2\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1f_2) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2), \quad \text{resp.} $$ $$ \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(0)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} ({\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2) + {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1)) - {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2). $$

nodes.name: Holomorphic part of $\partial^n R$ at $1/2$ via regularized integrals
nodes.statement_short: The holomorphic part of $\partial_s^n R(s,\varphi;f)$ at $1/2$ equals a regularized integral of $\varphi$ times an Eisenstein derivative, up to explicit $\lambda_F$-terms.
assumptions: Let notations be as in the previous proposition with $\Theta \leq -1/2$.
conclusions: $$ \left( \frac{\partial^n R}{\partial s^n} \right)^{{\rm hol}}(\frac{1}{2},\varphi;f) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f) - \sideset{}{_j'}\sum \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n+n_j)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_j f), $$

\begin{align*} \left( \frac{\partial^n R}{\partial s^n} \right)^{{\rm hol}}(\frac{1}{2},\varphi;f) &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f) - \sideset{}{_j'}\sum \frac{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n+n_j)}(0)}{\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(-1)}(0)} {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_j f) \\ &+ \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n)}(0) \cdot {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f \cdot (\xi^{-1} \circ \det)) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot (\xi \circ \det), \end{align*}
nodes.label: TripleToDouble

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement: The case (1) being simpler, we only give details for (2). By twisting, we may assume $\xi=1$. Let $s$ be small with $\Re s < 0$. The ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}(1/2+s,f)$ is given by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) := \sideset{}{_j} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f), $$ where the summation is over $j$ such that $\Re \alpha_j > -1$. Define $$ \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) := \sideset{}{_j'} \sum {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) + \sideset{}{_j^*} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) $$ where $\sideset{}{_j'} \sum$ is the summation as in the statement and $\sideset{}{_j^*} \sum$ is the rest. By the previous proposition, we have \begin{align*} R(\frac{1}{2}+s,\varphi;f) &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \\ &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) \\ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi. \end{align*} Since $\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(s)$ is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f)$, we can compare the holomorphic part of both sides and conclude by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) = \sideset{}{_j'} \sum \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n_j)}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_jf). $$
nodes.statement_short: Twist to $\xi=1$, write the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi{\rm E}(1/2+s,f)$ and its regularized variant, use Proposition 4.1, and compare holomorphic parts.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: The case (1) being simpler, we only give details for (2). By twisting, we may assume $\xi=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Treat (2) only; reduce to $\xi=1$ by twisting.

nodes.name: Residues
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be small with $\Re s < 0$. The ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}(1/2+s,f)$ is given by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) := \sideset{}{_j} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f), $$ where the summation is over $j$ such that $\Re \alpha_j > -1$. Define $$ \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) := \sideset{}{_j'} \sum {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) + \sideset{}{_j^*} \sum {\rm E}^{(n_j)}(s+1+\alpha_j, f_j f) $$ where $\sideset{}{_j'} \sum$ is the summation as in the statement and $\sideset{}{_j^*} \sum$ is the rest.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the ${\rm L}^2$-residue $\mathcal{E}(s)$ and its regularized variant.

nodes.name: Apply Proposition 4.1
nodes.statement: By the previous proposition, we have \begin{align*} R(\frac{1}{2}+s,\varphi;f) &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi \\ &= \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) - \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \left( \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) \right) \\ &\quad + \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f) \cdot \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply Proposition 4.1 and split off the regularizing term.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(s)$ is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of $\varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2}+s,f)$, we can compare the holomorphic part of both sides and conclude by $$ \mathcal{E}(s) - \mathcal{E}^{{\rm reg}}(s) = \sideset{}{_j'} \sum \lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^{(n_j)}(s) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_jf). $$
nodes.statement_short: Compare holomorphic parts.

nodes.name: A singular triple product formula
nodes.statement: Let $f_j \in \pi(1,1), j=1,2,3$. Then for any $n \in \ag{N}$ $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3) $$ is the sum of $$ \left( \frac{\partial^n R}{\partial s^n} \right)^{{\rm hol}}(\frac{1}{2}, {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2); f_3) $$ and a weighted sum with coefficients depending only on $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$ of $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(l)}f_1 \cdot f_2) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq 3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1\cdot f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(2,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}((f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 + f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1) \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(1,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+2; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0 f_1\cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq n \quad \& \quad l = n+1. $$
nodes.statement_short: $\int^{\rm reg}{\rm E}^*(0,f_1){\rm E}^*(0,f_2){\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(1/2,f_3)$ is a holomorphic-part term plus a $\lambda_F$-weighted sum of explicit ${\rm P}_K$ products.
conclusions: is the sum of $$ \left( \frac{\partial^n R}{\partial s^n} \right)^{{\rm hol}}(\frac{1}{2}, {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2); f_3) $$ and a weighted sum with coefficients depending only on $\lambda_{\mathbf{F}}(s)$ of $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0^{(l)}f_1 \cdot f_2) {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq 3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(f_1\cdot f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(2,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+3; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}((f_1 \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 + f_2 \mathcal{M}_0 f_1) \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq \max(1,n) \quad \& \quad l = n+2; $$ $$ {\rm P}_{\gp{K}}(\mathcal{M}_0 f_1\cdot \mathcal{M}_0 f_2 \cdot \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_{1/2}^{(l)} f_3), \quad 0 \leq l \leq n \quad \& \quad l = n+1. $$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3
nodes.statement: We shall only point out how the computation is effectuated, since the formulas are quite long. \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) &:= (\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2 \cdot \left\{ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(2)}(\frac{1}{2},f_1f_2) + \frac{1}{2} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(\frac{1}{2}, f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2 + \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2) \right. \\ &\quad\left. + \frac{1}{4} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\} \end{align*} is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of ${\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2)$. Let $\varphi := {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2)$, then we need to compute $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3) + \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3). $$ The first term is computed by Proposition \ref{TripleToDouble} (2), involving $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) = \frac{(\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2}{4} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2), $$ which is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisUnitary} (2). The second term is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisSing} (3).
nodes.statement_short: Sketch: subtract the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of ${\rm E}^*(0,f_1){\rm E}^*(0,f_2)$; the remainder is handled by Proposition 4.2 (2) and Theorem 3.4 (2), the residue term by Theorem 3.7 (3).

nodes.name: Residue
nodes.statement: We shall only point out how the computation is effectuated, since the formulas are quite long. \begin{align*} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) &:= (\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2 \cdot \left\{ {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(2)}(\frac{1}{2},f_1f_2) + \frac{1}{2} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(1)}(\frac{1}{2}, f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2 + \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot f_2) \right. \\ &\quad\left. + \frac{1}{4} {\rm E}^{{\rm reg}}(\frac{1}{2}, \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_1 \cdot \mathcal{M}_0^{(1)}f_2) \right\} \end{align*} is the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of ${\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write the ${\rm L}^2$-residue of the product of the two unitary Eisenstein series.

nodes.name: Split
nodes.statement: Let $\varphi := {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) - \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2)$, then we need to compute $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \varphi \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3) + \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} \mathcal{E}(f_1,f_2) \cdot {\rm E}^{{\rm reg},(n)}(\frac{1}{2},f_3). $$
nodes.statement_short: Split the integral into a remainder term and a residue term.

nodes.name: First term
nodes.statement: The first term is computed by Proposition \ref{TripleToDouble} (2), involving $$ \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]} \varphi = \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^*(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^*(0,f_2) = \frac{(\Lambda_{\mathbf{F}}^*)^2}{4} \int_{[{\rm PGL}_2]}^{{\rm reg}} {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_1) \cdot {\rm E}^{(1)}(0,f_2), $$ which is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisUnitary} (2).
nodes.statement_short: First term by Proposition 4.2 (2) and Theorem 3.4 (2).

nodes.name: Second term
nodes.statement: The second term is treated in Theorem \ref{RIPEisSing} (3).
nodes.statement_short: Second term by Theorem 3.7 (3).

nodes.name: Section $s_{\mathbf{F}}$ and characters trivial on its image
nodes.statement: Namely we fix a section $s_{\mathbf{F}}: \ag{R}_+ \to \mathbf{F}^{\times} \backslash \ag{A}^{\times}$ and assume the Hecke characters $\omega, \xi$ to be trivial on the image of $s_{\mathbf{F}}$.

nodes.name: Eisenstein series ${\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$
nodes.statement: We then have the definition of the Eisenstein series ${\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$ for $f \in V_{\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$.

nodes.name: Notation ${\rm E}(s,f)$
nodes.statement: We will sometimes omit $\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}$ and write ${\rm E}(s,f)$ when it is clear from the context.

nodes.name: Constant term ${\rm E}_{\gp{N}}$
nodes.statement: Precisely, we shall decompose it as $$ {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) = {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) + \left( {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) \right) \text{ with} $$ $$ {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) := \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}} {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(n(x)g) dx, n(x) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & x \\ & 1 \end{pmatrix} $$ and study the growth in $g$ of ${\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$ and ${\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$ separately, as well as all their derivatives with respect to $s$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the Eisenstein series into its constant term ${\rm E}_N$ (integral over $N$) and the non-constant part.

nodes.name: Whittaker function $W(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)$
nodes.statement: We focus on $$ {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) - {\rm E}_{\gp{N}}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbf{F}^{\times}} W(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(a(\alpha)g) \text{ with } a(\alpha)=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \\ & 1 \end{pmatrix} $$ $$ \text{and} \quad W(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(g) = \int_{\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}} \psi(-x) {\rm E}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};f)(n(x)g) dx, $$ where $\psi$ is the standard additive character of $\mathbf{F} \backslash \ag{A}$.
nodes.statement_short: The non-constant part is a sum over $\mathbf{F}^\times$ of translates of the Whittaker function $W$, the $\psi$-Fourier coefficient of ${\rm E}$.

nodes.name: Godement section $f_{\Phi}$
nodes.statement: If $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\ag{A}^2)$ is a Schwartz function, we can define the following (non flat) section in $V_{s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$ $$ f_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};g) = \xi(\det g)\norm[\det g]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{1}{2}+s} \int_{\ag{A}^{\times}} \Phi((0,t)g) \omega^{-1}\xi^2(t) \norm[t]_{\ag{A}}^{1+2s} d^{\times}t $$ first defined for $\Re s > 0$ then meromorphically continued to $s \in \ag{C}$.
nodes.statement_short: Non-flat section built from a Schwartz function $\Phi$ on $\mathbb{A}^2$ by a Tate-type integral.

nodes.name: Choice of $\Phi$ attached to $f$
nodes.statement:
Given $f \in V_{0,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}}^{\infty}$, we want to give an explicit $\Phi$ associated with $f$. For simplicity of notations, we may assume $f$ to be a pure tensor. We then construct $\Phi = \otimes_v' \Phi_v$ place by place: 
oindent (1) At $\mathbf{F}_v = \ag{C}$ resp. $\mathbf{F}_v = \ag{R}$ and for $f_v$ spherical resp. not spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ using the construction in \cite[Lemma 3.5 (1)]{Wu5} resp. \cite[Lemma 3.8 (1)]{Wu5} for spherical resp. smooth functions. 
oindent (2) At $v < \infty$ and for $f_v$ not spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ by $$ \Phi_v((0,1) \kappa) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\xi_v(\det \kappa)^{-1}f_v(\kappa), \kappa \in \gp{K}_v 	ext{ i.e.} $$ $$ \Phi_v(ux,u) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\omega_v \xi_v^2(u) f_v  egin{pmatrix} 1 & \ x & 1 \end{pmatrix},  orall u \in \mathfrak{o}_v^{	imes}, x \in \mathfrak{o}_v; $$ $$ \Phi_v(u,uy) = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v)\omega_v \xi_v^2(u) f_v  egin{pmatrix} & -1 \ 1 & y \end{pmatrix},  orall u \in \mathfrak{o}_v^{	imes}, y \in \varpi_v \mathfrak{o}_v; $$ and $\Phi_v(x,y)=0$ for $\max(
orm[x]_v,
orm[y]_v) 
eq 1$. 
oindent (3) At $v < \infty$ and for $f_v$ spherical, we choose $\Phi_v$ by $$ \Phi_v = \mathbf{C}(\psi_v) \cdot f_v(1) \cdot 1_{\mathfrak{o}_v^2}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Place-by-place construction of a Schwartz function $\Phi$ whose section $f_\Phi$ is a multiple of $f_s$.

nodes.name: Relation between $f_{\Phi}$ and the flat section
nodes.statement: Let $S=S(f)$ be the set of places $v$ such that $f_v$ is not spherical. Then we get \begin{equation} f_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};g) = {\rm D}(\mathbf{F})^{\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda^S(1+2s,\omega^{-1}\xi^2) \prod_{\substack{v \in S \\ v \mid \infty}} K_{v,a_v}(s,\omega_v^{-1}\xi_v^2) \cdot f_s(g). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $f_\Phi$ is the flat section $f_s$ times a partial completed $L$-function and archimedean factors.
assumptions: Let $S=S(f)$ be the set of places $v$ such that $f_v$ is not spherical.
conclusions: f_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};g) = {\rm D}(\mathbf{F})^{\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda^S(1+2s,\omega^{-1}\xi^2) \prod_{\substack{v \in S \\ v \mid \infty}} K_{v,a_v}(s,\omega_v^{-1}\xi_v^2) \cdot f_s(g).

nodes.name: Relation of sections (5.1)
nodes.statement: f_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1};g) = {\rm D}(\mathbf{F})^{\frac{1}{2}}\Lambda^S(1+2s,\omega^{-1}\xi^2) \prod_{\substack{v \in S \\ v \mid \infty}} K_{v,a_v}(s,\omega_v^{-1}\xi_v^2) \cdot f_s(g).
nodes.label: RelSec

nodes.name: Integral representation of $W_{\Phi}$ (5.2)
nodes.statement: W_{\Phi}(s,\xi,\omega\xi^{-1}; g) = \xi(\det g)\norm[\det g]_{\ag{A}}^{\frac{1}{2}+s} \int_{\ag{A}^{\times}} \Four[2]{{\rm R}(g).\Phi}(t,\frac{1}{t}) \omega^{-1}\xi^2(t)\norm[t]_{\ag{A}}^{2s} d^{\times}t,
nodes.statement_short: Whittaker function of $f_\Phi$ as a Mellin-type integral of a partial Fourier transform of ${\rm R}(g).\Phi$.
nodes.label: SchWhi

nodes.name: Local integral representation of $W_{\Phi}$

nodes.name: Support, additive and multiplicative invariance indices
nodes.statement: Let $d \geq 1$ be an integer. For any $\Phi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbf{F}^d)$ we define its \emph{support index} $D(\Phi) \in \ag{Z}$, \emph{additive invariance index} $\delta(\Phi) \in \ag{Z}$ and \emph{multiplicative invariance index} $m(\Phi) \in \ag{N}$ as follows. \begin{itemize} \item[(1)] $D(\Phi)$ is the largest integer $D$ such that $$ \Phi(\vec{x}) \neq 0 \Rightarrow \vec{x} \in \mathfrak{p}^D \times \cdots \times \mathfrak{p}^D. $$ \item[(2)] $\delta(\Phi)$ is the smallest integer $\delta$ such that $$ \Phi(\vec{x}+\vec{t}) = \Phi(\vec{x}), \forall \vec{x} \in \mathbf{F}^d, \vec{t} \in \mathfrak{p}^{\delta} \times \cdots \times \mathfrak{p}^{\delta}. $$ \item[(3)] $m(\Phi)$ is the smallest integer $m \geq 0$ such that for any $\kappa \in {\rm GL}_d(\mathfrak{o})$ with $\kappa-1 \in {\rm M}_d(\mathfrak{p}^m)$ $$ {\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi(\vec{x}) = \Phi(\vec{x}.\kappa) = \Phi(\vec{x}), \forall \vec{x} \in \mathbf{F}^d. $$ \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $D(\Phi)$: largest support level; $\delta(\Phi)$: smallest additive invariance level; $m(\Phi)$: smallest level of ${\rm GL}_d(\mathfrak{o})$-invariance.

nodes.name: Relations between the indices $D$, $\delta$, $m$
nodes.statement: The three indices satisfy the following relations. \begin{itemize} \item[(0)] $m(\Phi) \leq \delta(\Phi)-D(\Phi)$. \item[(1)] For any $\kappa \in {\rm GL}_d(\mathfrak{o})$, we have $D({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=D(\Phi)$, $\delta({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=\delta(\Phi)$ and $m({\rm R}(\kappa).\Phi)=m(\Phi)$. \item[(2)] Let $\Four{\cdot}$ denote the Fourier transform $$ \Four{\Phi}(\vec{x}) = \int_{\mathbf{F}^d} \Phi(\vec{y}) \psi(-\vec{y}.\vec{x}) d\vec{y}. $$ Then we have $$ D(\Phi)+\delta(\Four{\Phi}) = \delta(\Phi) + D(\Four{\Phi}) = -\mathfrak{c}(\psi). $$ \item[(3)] More generally, let $I = \{ i_1, \cdots, i_j \} \subset \{ 1, \dots, d \}$. We define the partial Fourier transform $\Four[I]{\cdot} = \Four[i_1]{\Four[i_2]{ \cdots \Four[i_j]{\cdot}}}$. Then we have $$ \delta(\Four[I]{\Phi})) \leq \max(\delta(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-D(\Phi)); $$ $$ D(\Four[I]{\Phi}) \geq \min(D(\Phi), -\mathfrak{c}(\psi)-\delta(\Phi)). $$ \end{itemize}
